questions.q: What is the role of an emulator in retro gaming on the Raspberry Pi?
choices: A program that mimics an old games console in software so game files designed for that console can run on the Pi.
A tool that stores game files on the microSD card so they load faster.
A service that connects your Pi to the internet to download games legally.
A converter that transforms modern game files into a format the original console hardware can read.
questions.explain: An emulator mimics the original hardware in software — it tricks game files into thinking they are running on the real console. It has nothing to do with storage speed or internet downloads.

questions.q: Why does this guide recommend Batocera over RetroPie for absolute beginners?
choices: Batocera runs on the same microSD card as Raspberry Pi OS, saving space.
Batocera is cheaper to download than RetroPie.
Batocera is a complete, standalone operating system that installs quickly, detects controllers automatically, and needs almost no configuration.
Batocera supports more consoles than RetroPie does.
questions.explain: Batocera is recommended because it is a plug-and-play experience with automatic controller detection and minimal setup, flashed to a separate card. RetroPie adds gaming on top of an existing Pi OS installation, which requires more manual steps.

questions.q: You copy a NES ROM file into the correct Batocera folder but it does not appear in the game list. What should you do first?
choices: Delete the file and copy it again using a USB drive instead.
Pair your controller via Bluetooth before the game list will refresh.
Restart the Pi to trigger an automatic scan.
Press Start, choose Game Settings, then Update Game Lists.
questions.explain: After copying new ROM files to Batocera you must manually trigger a refresh via Start > Game Settings > Update Game Lists. The game list does not update automatically, and restarting the Pi is not needed.

questions.q: Which hotkey shortcut saves a save state to slot 1 while a game is running in Batocera?
choices: Hotkey + L1
Hotkey + R1
Hotkey + Start
Hotkey + B
questions.explain: Hotkey + R1 saves a save state to slot 1. Hotkey + L1 loads the state, Hotkey + Start quits back to EmulationStation, and Hotkey + B opens the RetroArch menu.

questions.q: The Pi 5 has no 3.5 mm headphone socket. Which of the following is NOT a valid way to get audio from Batocera on a Pi 5?
choices: Using the HDMI cable to send audio to a monitor or TV.
Plugging a USB audio adapter into a USB port on the Pi.
Connecting a 3.5 mm cable directly to the Pi's GPIO pins.
Pairing Bluetooth headphones via Controller and Bluetooth Settings.
questions.explain: The chapter lists three valid audio options for the Pi 5: HDMI, a USB audio adapter, and Bluetooth. GPIO pins do not provide an audio output on the Pi 5 and this is not a supported method.
